start.title: Where to begin
nodes: Choose the workspace for the task you have been given.
Use the account assigned to that service.
Look for the queue or programme you expect.

services.title: Choose a starting point
nodes: Find Registry checks and approval tasks.
Find list preparation, payment and reporting guides.

lifecycle.title: How a household record reaches a payment decision
nodes: A household record is captured and reviewed.
Programme staff check eligibility and calculate benefits.
An approved list goes for payment. Staff check the bank outcome.

household-registration.title: From household interview to registration
nodes: Record the applicant, household members and location.
Check the roster and declaration, then keep the case reference.
Correct the same record if returned. After approval, check its Registry connection.

registration-review.title: What a reviewer decides
nodes: Choose a registration awaiting your review.
Check each member and any earlier correction request.
Approve a complete registration or explain what the applicant needs to change.

master-registry.title: From draft to published record
nodes: Captures details and submits the record.
Checks the submission and sends an approved case to Level 2.
Checks the earlier decision and publishes an approved record.

registry-review.title: What happens to a submission
nodes: The first reviewer checks the record and possible matches.
The second reviewer checks the submission and the first decision.
Final approval makes the record available to the Registry Officer.

data-imports.title: How a file becomes Registry records
nodes: Validates the rows, resolves issues and requests approval.
Checks included and excluded rows before deciding.
Transfers the approved batch and checks the Registry receipt.

offline-collection.title: From an offline interview to the Registry
nodes: Load the assigned form on the authorised device.
Complete and save the interview on the device.
Send the form, then check the matching Registry intake reference.

social-registry.title: Finding an existing record
nodes: Use the existing Social Registry for its earlier records.
Search the relevant individuals or groups.
Review identifying details and the associated group or household.

beneficiary-portal.title: Three places to check
nodes: Find your registration and its review status.
Follow a programme application by its reference.
Check which approved entitlements are available.

programme-setup.title: What a programme needs before a cycle
nodes: Choose the registry and approved eligibility criteria.
Check the benefit code, unit and quantity.
Confirm the staff roles and delivery route for the programme.

cycles-and-lists.title: How a cycle becomes a list
nodes: Check the registration window and disbursement schedule.
Apply the programme criteria to its target records.
Compare the included people, benefit amounts and total for this revision.

pbms-approvals.title: Who reviews a payment list
nodes: Starts approval for the completed list.
Finance checks amounts. Audit then checks the evidence and history.
Reviews the earlier decisions and records the final decision.

payment-and-reconciliation.title: Follow the payment evidence
nodes: Payment confirms the verified list and sponsor bank route.
The batch report tracks the instructions sent towards the bank.
Compare the envelope report with the bank statement for each affected instruction.

reversals-and-exceptions.title: When another reversal appears
nodes: Match the payment and both statement entries.
Treat an identical repeat as duplicate evidence. Refer a different amount to Finance.
Audit preserves both entries and the decision under the same reference.

bridge-and-mapper.title: Where the instruction goes
nodes: Resolve the beneficiary reference and track dispatch to the bank.
Checks the returned statement against the envelope and batch.

beneficiary-admin.title: From programme setup to the applicant view
nodes: Find the beneficiary-facing programme in administration.
Review visibility, application fields and related records.
Verify what an applicant can see in the corresponding programme.

access.title: How staff reach their work
nodes: Sign in with the assigned staff account.
Open the service for the task.
Check the queue, registry scope or programme membership inside that service.

approvals.title: How to follow an approval request
nodes: Use the originating record or request reference.
Read the assigned reviewer and recorded decisions.
Check whether the originating service received the result.

master-data.title: Read the location hierarchy
nodes: Choose the parent area in Nigeria.
Choose an LGA within that state or territory.
Choose a ward within the selected LGA.

partners.title: From request to partner record
nodes: Check the organisation and partner reference.
Read the onboarding or change request and its status.
Use the partner record to check its keys and history.

consent.title: What to check before sharing information
nodes: Identify who is requesting the information.
Check the relevant data and sharing policy.
Read the recorded approval or decision for that request.

analytics.title: How to read a reported count
nodes: Check the programme, period and geography.
Record the filters and reporting date with any authorised export.

phase-one.title: Follow a sandbox case
nodes: Start with an example household or programme.
Inspect the grievance, attendance or field record.
Read the recorded status and verification history.

support.title: Finding help for the screen in front of you
nodes: Select Help, or the information icon beside a field.
Read the steps for the current task and role.
Keep the guide title, action, status and a non-sensitive reference.

jos-family-support.title: Follow the Jos example
nodes: Start with the sample household in the demonstration.
Follow the eligibility and conditionality decisions.
Trace the approved outcome into the example payment report.

field-interaction-preview.title: How a sample visit works
nodes: Use a sample record to explore the form.
Move between the area, household needs and review.
For connected work, confirm the submission in the Registry.

territorial-atlas.title: How to read an area in the atlas
nodes: Select the state or other available geography.
Use the comparison measure that answers your question.
Check the reference date before comparing areas.

partial-payment.title: Reading a partial payment
nodes: Keep its envelope and batch references.
Identify which have settled, which are outstanding and which reversed.
Finance verifies the affected instructions before an authorised follow-up.

missing-log.title: How to read a missing or restored log
nodes: The Registry has already stored the row.
Keep the original reference. A matching alternate correction stays on hold.
Refresh the original receipt and check the restoration event in Activity.

returned-list.title: How a returned list moves forward
nodes: Open the returned list and identify the requested change.
Programme Admin corrects the affected entries and records why.
Payment checks the correction. The new revision starts again at Finance.

separate-import.title: Two files from the same connection
nodes: Use the batch reference to choose the original import.
Fetch a new CSV when a separate import is intended.
Check its previous batch reference to see which original it follows.

duplicate-check.title: Review a possible match
nodes: Find the proposed match and open its comparison.
Check the identity and household information on both records.
Follow the assigned review procedure. Escalate an unclear match.

reversal-count-check.title: When the reversal counts disagree
nodes: Keep the list revision, envelope and batch references together.
Finance checks whether both entries refer to the same bank movement.
For a closed case, hold payment activity while the discrepancy is reviewed.

sponsor-route.title: Who sets the bank route?
nodes: Confirm the programme and the verified list revision.
Choose the approved sponsor bank and save the payment route.
Check the saved route before submitting the verified list.

case-closure.title: Who closes a payment case?
nodes: Compare the payments and reversals with the bank statement and record the balance.
Trace each revision and decision back to its supporting evidence.
Enter the closure reason, date and outcome under the existing case reference.

publish-guidance.title: How a draft becomes published guidance
nodes: Write the guidance and submit it for review.
A different person checks the draft and can return it with a reason.
An authorised supervisor publishes the reviewed version.
